correctness.rationale: The finite-sample conditional law follows exactly from Bernoulli exchangeability. The conditional mean is obtained from first- and second-order hypergeometric moments. An exact centered decomposition reduces the asymptotics to a bounded triangular array; the degenerate quadratic remainder has variance O(log(k)/k^2). The coefficient-square Riemann sums converge to 5 p^2 before and p^2 after plug-in prevalence adjustment, yielding variances 5 p^3(1-p) and p^3(1-p). Exact-enumeration and algebraic checks in verify.py independently replay all finite identities used by the proof. The asymptotic claim is restricted to fixed p in (0,1).

broader_coverage.reasoning: Su–Yuan–Zhu use a multinomial score-strata model and a delta-method AP variance for diagnostic ranking, not the top-k iid Bernoulli random-order statistic. Smucker–Allan–Carterette compare paired system-level significance tests for MAP differences, rather than an exact one-sample random-ranking null conditional on total relevance.

originality.rationale: The closest paper gives exact first and second moments for the same online Bernoulli AP@k statistic and explicitly leaves statistical testing for future work; it does not state the prevalence-conditioned pivot, either Gaussian limit, or the 4+1 leading variance split. Fixed-count random-baseline and general AP asymptotic-variance papers cover related objects but do not imply the stated constants without a new AP@k-specific decomposition. The novelty claim excludes the classical fact that iid Bernoulli variables conditional on their total are uniformly distributed over fixed-count strings.
residual_risks: Conditioning iid Bernoulli variables on their total is classical and is not part of the novelty claim.
A specialized information-retrieval testing paper not surfaced by the searches could contain an equivalent AP@k conditional calibration.
The Gaussian limit may be obtainable from a general U-statistic or triangular-array theorem, but no inspected source states the AP@k constants 5 and 1 or the 4+1 variance split.

value.rationale: The result directly turns the motivating random-baseline moment formulas into a nuisance-free finite-sample ordering test and quantifies which part of AP@k null variability is due to prevalence rather than ordering. The 4+1 split is operationally meaningful: conditioning removes four fifths of the first-order null variance while deliberately changing the target from overall relevance to ordering conditional on count. This addresses the source’s stated testing direction without claiming a general retrieval-system testing theory.
